allowed_hosts: each user@host entry in REMOTE_SERVERS (empty in both repository config templates)
allowed_write_paths: remote temporary directory created by mktemp -d

scripts.purpose: Installs every local/*.sh script into /usr/local/bin, deploys remote/*.sh scripts over SSH to configured hosts, and installs the shared config template while migrating a legacy config.conf. Arguments are ignored; settings come from the config file and environment. It also copies remote/config to each host's ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/user-scripts/config (or config.new when one exists) so the remote/ scripts source server settings. The local config template comes from local/config; a legacy config.conf is migrated when no current config exists.

environment.name: SUDO_USER
environment.description: Invoking user whose home directory and numeric uid/gid own the deployed config; falls back to the current user.

environment.name: XDG_CONFIG_HOME
environment.description: Base directory for the user-scripts config directory.

environment.name: USER_SCRIPTS_CONFIG
environment.description: Explicit config supplying remote deployment settings; takes precedence over installed, legacy, and repository configs.

environment.name: REMOTE_SERVERS
environment.description: Array of user@host targets from the config; an empty list disables remote deployment.

environment.name: REMOTE_INSTALL_DIR
environment.description: Destination directory for deployed scripts on each remote host.

environment.name: SSH_TIMEOUT
environment.description: Non-interactive ssh/scp connect timeout in seconds.

write_paths: remote temporary directory created by mktemp -d
${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/user-scripts/config or config.new on each host (from remote/config)
network_hosts: each user@host entry in REMOTE_SERVERS (ssh and scp)

exit_codes.meaning: All local scripts were installed (individual local failures are reported only), the local config was deployed, and every configured remote deployment (scripts and remote/config) succeeded; no remote hosts is also success.
Not run as root, an explicitly requested config file is unreadable, or one or more remote deployments (scripts or remote/config) failed.
